page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 60 dedicated physical cores and 60 vCPUs, operating with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The underlying x86_64 architecture includes an L1d cache of 32 KB, an L2 cache of 0.5 MB, and an L3 cache of 32 MB. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% at 141,982.77. Single-core stress-ng performance is also strong, placing in the top 25% at 2,693.79. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for cached small blocks at 6,846.14 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier at 141.75 GB/sec and 64.61 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 520.43 GB/sec and Geekbench multi-core scores of 17,297.0 further confirm its high parallel processing efficiency.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-60 offers high resource density and dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, making it highly efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. However, the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration limits its suitability for large-scale deep learning training or high-I/O database tasks. It is highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and moderate LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing for medium-sized models.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 60 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 240.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core, and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. The instance exhibits top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng benchmarks, and strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. While uncached memory bandwidth and large-model LLM text generation represent performance tradeoffs, the server is highly cost-efficient for parallel processing. It is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads, software development pipelines, database hosting, and moderate-scale language model inference.
